then I will give you your rains in their season, and the land shall yield its increase, and the trees of the field shall yield their fruit.
Your threshing shall continue until the vintage, and the vintage shall continue until the sowing time. You shall eat your bread to the full, and dwell in your land safely.
“‘I will give peace in the land, and you shall lie down, and no one will make you afraid. I will remove evil animals out of the land, neither shall the sword go through your land.
You shall chase your enemies, and they shall fall before you by the sword.
Five of you shall chase a hundred, and a hundred of you shall chase ten thousand; and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.
“‘I will have respect for you, make you fruitful, multiply you, and will establish my covenant with you.
You shall eat old supplies long kept, and you shall move out the old because of the new.
I will set my tent among you, and my soul won’t abhor you.
I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you will be my people.
b: This passage is a clear promise: “If you… then I will…” God does not suppress people with law; he builds a relationship through covenant. Obedience is not a bargain but a life aligned with God’s heart. When people return to their rightful place and let God be God, blessing flows naturally.

Blessing is not only material abundance but also peace and victory. Rains in season, produce, and safe dwelling represent provision in daily life; chasing enemies represents spiritual protection. When God is present, even five can overcome a hundred. Strength does not lie in numbers but in whether we walk with God.

Most precious are the last two verses: “I will set my tent among you… I will be your God.” True blessing is not grain or victory, but God’s presence. God desires to dwell among his people and walk among them. This is the core from the tabernacle of the old covenant to Immanuel in the new: God dwelling with people.
a: Respond to the covenant with obedience
Let God’s word be the standard for your life.
Stand in peace
Believe God is your protection and your victory.
Treasure God’s presence
More than outward blessings, long for God to walk among you.
q: Am I pursuing blessings, or pursuing God’s presence?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for making a covenant with us and being willing to walk among us. Help me to obey Your word and not turn from Your way. Let me find peace and victory in Your presence, and let my life be a testimony that glorifies You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I obey God’s word and live in his presence; he is my God and I am his people.

t: Christ as the Greatest Treasure
v: though I myself might have confidence even in the flesh. If any other man thinks that he has confidence in the flesh, I yet more:
circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; concerning the law, a Pharisee;
concerning zeal, persecuting the assembly; concerning the righteousness which is in the law, found blameless.
However, I consider those things that were gain to me as a loss for Christ.

Yes most certainly, and I count all things to be a loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus, my Lord, for whom I suffered the loss of all things, and count them nothing but refuse, that I may gain Christ
and be found in him, not having a righteousness of my own, that which is of the law, but that which is through faith in Christ, the righteousness which is from God by faith,
that I may know him and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, becoming conformed to his death,
if by any means I may attain to the resurrection from the dead.
b: Paul first lists the background he could boast of: ancestry, religion, zeal, and works; he had it all. By fleshly standards he certainly stood on solid ground. Yet he discovered that if all this becomes what we rely on, it becomes a hindrance. When people exalt themselves, it is hard to truly know Christ. The glory of the flesh actually obscures the heavenly light.

“What things were gain to me, these have I counted loss.” This is a reversal of mindset. It is not that those achievements are wrong in themselves, but that they cannot replace Christ. Only when Paul saw the glory of Jesus did he understand what the “greatest treasure” is. If Jesus is the focus, everything else is merely background. If Jesus is not the greatest treasure, no amount of possessions can fill the emptiness.

What Paul longed for was not only to be justified but to “know Christ.” Knowing is not just head knowledge but a life connection: experiencing the power of his resurrection, and being willing to share in his sufferings. It is a road from self-centeredness to Christ-centeredness. Giving up self is not loss but gaining true life.
a: Examine what you rely on
Do I still try to prove myself by background, ability, or achievements?
Redefine your treasure
Let knowing Christ be the highest value in your life.
Die with him, live with him
Walk with the Lord in both good times and bad.
q: In my heart, what is the true “greatest treasure”?
pr: Heavenly Father, shine Your light on me so that I see that true value is found in Christ. Help me lay down self-boasting and count knowing the Lord as my greatest treasure. Let me live in the power of the resurrection and grow mature as I walk with the Lord. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Christ is the greatest treasure of my life; I give up boasting, only to gain him.

t: Words That Build Up or Tear Down
v: By the blessing of the upright, the city is exalted, but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.
One who despises his neighbor is void of wisdom, but a man of understanding holds his peace.
One who brings gossip betrays a confidence, but one who is of a trustworthy spirit is one who keeps a secret.
b: This passage reminds us that the rise and fall of a city depends not only on its systems and economy, but on the mouths of its people. The blessing of the upright lifts a city up; the words of the wicked can bring it down. Words carry power. They can build, and they can tear down. When a heart is set toward God, blessing flows naturally from the mouth; when a heart drifts from God, the mouth fills with destruction.

The second verse says that despising a neighbor is a lack of wisdom. Much of the harm we do is not done with swords but with one careless, dismissive word. The man of understanding chooses silence, not out of cowardice but out of self-control. A truly mature person is not quick to comment or careless to criticize. Knowing when to close our mouth is part of wisdom.

Finally, the passage speaks of the “tale-bearer” who reveals secrets. Gossip is like fire: once it spreads, it is hard to call back. A faithful person, by contrast, conceals a matter and does not use another’s weakness as something to talk about. Guarding our tongue is guarding our relationships. When we let Jesus be King in our hearts, our words naturally become a blessing rather than a wound.
a: Speak blessing
Deliberately use your words to build people up rather than criticize them.
Learn restraint
In the heat of the moment, be silent first and let the Holy Spirit lead you.
Keep confidences
Be faithful with the trust others place in you; do not gossip or expose their weaknesses.
q: Are my words lifting people up, or tearing them down?
pr: Heavenly Father, cleanse my mouth so that I never hurt others with my words. Teach me to be quiet in the moment of impulse and to guard my tongue in the midst of gossip. Let my words be a blessing that builds relationships and glorifies Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: My mouth speaks blessing; I will not gossip or tear down. I let God’s wisdom govern my words.

t: Finishing the Race
v: For I am already being offered, and the time of my departure has come.
I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.
From now on, the crown of righteousness is stored up for me, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will give to me on that day; and not to me only, but also to all those who have loved his appearing.
b: Paul wrote these words at the very end of his life. He knew he would die as a martyr, yet there was no regret or fear. Like wine poured out on an altar, he gave himself gladly. When a life is lived for the Lord, departing this world is not a loss but a completion. What matters is not how long we live, but whether we are faithful.

“I have fought the good fight.” The life of faith is both a battle and a journey. The fight must be fought, the race must be run, and the faith must be kept. It is not a short sprint but a long, steady endurance. Success is not measured by outward achievements but by whether we have held fast to the faith. Faithfulness matters more than fame.

Finally, Paul looks ahead to the “crown of righteousness.” This crown is not earthly glory but the Lord’s own personal approval. Even more precious, this promise belongs not to Paul alone but to “all those who have loved his appearing.” When we love the Lord’s return, the direction of our whole life is drawn toward eternity. When our eyes are fixed on that day, today’s hardships no longer feel so heavy.
a: Pour yourself out gladly
Offer your life as a sacrifice and live for the Lord.
Hold on faithfully
In good times and bad, keep the faith you have believed.
Love his appearing
Make eternity your goal and adjust today’s choices accordingly.
q: If today were the summing up of my life, could I say, “I have kept the faith”?
pr: Heavenly Father, help me to be faithful to the end in the limited years I have. Let me fight the good fight, finish the race, and keep the faith. Make me love the appearing of the Lord and long for the crown of righteousness. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I run faithfully and keep the faith; the crown of righteousness is stored up for me.

t: Don’t Just Gaze at the Sky—Be a Witness
v: Therefore, when they had come together, they asked him, “Lord, are you now restoring the kingdom to Israel?”
He said to them, “It isn’t for you to know times or seasons which the Father has set within his own authority.
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you. You will be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth.”
When he had said these things, as they were looking, he was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight.
While they were looking steadfastly into the sky as he went, behold, two men stood by them in white clothing,
who also said, “You men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into the sky? This Jesus, who was received up from you into the sky, will come back in the same way as you saw him going into the sky.”
b: The disciples were concerned with “When will the kingdom be restored?” But Jesus turned their focus to “What will you do?” The timing of the future is in the Father’s authority, but today’s mission is in our hands. Faith is not about guessing dates; it is about being faithful to the One who sends us.

“The Holy Spirit has come upon you … you will receive power.” This power is not for our own glory, but for being the Lord’s witnesses. From Jerusalem to the ends of the earth, our influence reaches from near to far. When the Holy Spirit is in charge, our lives become vessels of the Kingdom of God.

The disciples gazed at the sky, and the angels reminded them not to stay there. The Lord will surely return, but until then, we must act. We look to the Lord without standing still; we wait for the Lord without being idle. Our focus is on Jesus, and our feet are on the earth.
a: Focus on the mission
Ask less about the timing and respond more to the calling.
Rely on the Holy Spirit
Let the Holy Spirit be the source of your power.
Act with hope
Be faithful while you wait, and move forward in hope.
q: Am I only gazing at the sky, while neglecting the task God has given me on earth?
pr: Heavenly Father, help me not merely to gaze at the sky, but to be a faithful witness on earth. Give me the power of the Holy Spirit so that I may live out the gospel. As I hope for the Lord’s return, let me also eagerly respond to Your sending. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I have received the power of the Holy Spirit; I bear witness to the Lord on earth, and I wait for his return with hope.

t: True Repentance Brings Restoration
v: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the children of Israel: ‘When a man or woman commits any sin that men commit, so as to trespass against the LORD, and that soul is guilty,
then he shall confess his sin which he has done; and he shall make restitution for his guilt in full, add to it the fifth part of it, and give it to him in respect of whom he has been guilty.

But if the man has no kinsman to whom restitution may be made for the guilt, the restitution for guilt which is made to the LORD shall be the priest’s, in addition to the ram of the atonement, by which atonement shall be made for him.
Every heave offering of all the holy things of the children of Israel, which they present to the priest, shall be his.
Every man’s holy things shall be his; whatever any man gives the priest, it shall be his.’”
b: This passage shows us an important principle: sin is not only an offense against people, but against God. Even “any sin that men commit” is taken seriously by God. The essence of sin is turning away from God’s heart, with self-centeredness taking the place of God as King. So repentance begins with confession, not with cover-up.

God does not only ask us to confess our sin; he also wants relationships restored. “Make restitution in full, and add a fifth part to it.” True repentance is more than saying the words “I was wrong”; it is a willingness to pay the price to repair what was broken. This shows a humble heart, willing to return to its rightful place so that God’s justice and love can flow again.

Finally, the holy things given to the priest remind us that everything ultimately belongs to God. Repentance does not merely solve a problem; it hands sovereignty back to God. When a person turns from self-centeredness to God-centeredness, life is realigned and relationships are restored.
a: Confess courageously
Do not run or make excuses; honestly face your own offenses.
Repair proactively
Be willing to make amends and restore the relationship, not just apologize.
Give sovereignty to God
Let God be King in your life so that everything is realigned.
q: Does my repentance stay on my lips, or does it truly bring change and restoration?
pr: Heavenly Father, shine Your light into my heart so I can see where I have offended You. Give me courage to confess, and humility to repair relationships. Help me no longer to live for myself, but to let You be King in my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I repent honestly and restore relationships, and I let God be King in my life.

t: Humility in the Midst of Grace
v: Then David the king went in and sat before the LORD; and he said, “Who am I, LORD God, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?
This was a small thing in your eyes, O God, but you have spoken of your servant’s house for a great while to come, and have respected me according to the standard of a man of high degree, LORD God.
What can David say yet more to you concerning the honor which is done to your servant? For you know your servant.
LORD, for your servant’s sake, and according to your own heart, you have done all this greatness, to make known all these great things.
LORD, there is no one like you, neither is there any God besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

What one nation on the earth is like your people Israel, whom God went to redeem to himself for a people, to make you a name by great and awesome things, in driving out nations from before your people whom you redeemed out of Egypt?
For you made your people Israel your own people forever; and you, LORD, became their God.
b: David did not stand and boast before God; he “sat before Yahweh.” From the position of a king, he returned to the position of a servant. He said, “Who am I?” This was not low self-esteem, but an understanding of grace. A person who truly knows God does not exalt himself; he is filled with wonder at God’s grace.

God’s promise to David was enormous, yet David knew that none of it was because he deserved it, but “according to your own heart.” The essence of grace is God’s initiative of love and choosing. When we see this, we no longer grasp at glory but give everything back to God. Humility is not belittling ourselves; it is putting God first.

David looked beyond his own blessing to God’s redemption of all Israel. He turned from the personal to the Kingdom of God. When God is our God and we are his people, that is the greatest identity and honor. The focus of life is no longer “What have I received?” but “What has God accomplished?”
a: Return often to the Lord’s presence
Set aside status and achievements, and be humble and still before God.
Remember the source of grace
Acknowledge that everything is God’s heart and God’s work.
Turn toward God’s Kingdom
Look beyond personal blessing to God’s glory and plan.
q: Am I humble in the midst of grace, or am I unknowingly exalting myself in it?
pr: Heavenly Father, who am I that You have treated me so kindly? Keep me humble always, and let me never take Your glory. Let me live within Your heart, so that all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Everything is God’s grace. I am humble before him and give him all the glory.

t: The Joy of Being Found
v: “Or what woman, if she had ten drachma coins, if she lost one drachma coin, wouldn’t light a lamp, sweep the house, and seek diligently until she found it?
When she has found it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma which I had lost!’
Even so, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner repenting.”
b: This parable shows us the heart of God: he is a God who seeks. The lost coin cannot come back by itself, but the woman lights a lamp, sweeps the house, and searches carefully until she finds it. This is no casual looking; it is a heartfelt search. God is the same toward every person; no one is overlooked.

When the coin is found, the point is not that its value has increased, but that something has been restored. The woman rejoices and even invites others to celebrate. Jesus says it is the same in heaven: when one sinner repents, there is great joy. What God values is not numbers but each and every soul.

Repentance is not being scolded; it is being found. When we are willing to turn back, we enter into God’s joy. This joy is not forced; it is the joy of restoration. When a person leaves self behind and returns to God’s embrace, he passes from lost to found, from darkness into light.
a: Respond to God’s search
When God shines his light, don’t run away; be willing to repent and turn to him.
Value every person
Learn to see the worth of every soul through God’s eyes.
Become one who seeks
Work with God to care for and bring back those who are lost.
q: Am I willing to be found by God, and willing to become one who seeks others?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for not giving up on me but seeking me again and again. When I was lost, You still waited for me to return. Help me respond to Your love, and give me Your heart to seek those who are lost. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God searched for me and I have been found by him. I also work with him to bring back those who are lost.

t: You Are Precious in God’s Eyes
v: For he will deliver the needy when he cries; the poor, who has no helper.
He will have pity on the poor and needy. He will save the souls of the needy.
He will redeem their soul from oppression and violence. Their blood will be precious in his sight.
b: This passage shows us God’s heart: he has special concern for the helpless. When the needy cry out, he answers; when no one else will help, he steps in himself. This is not an indifferent God, but a God who hears the cry. People may overlook us, but God never does.

God does not only see; he acts. He has pity, he saves, he redeems. Whether our need is material or the pain of oppression, God cares. He does not watch from a distance but reaches out his hand himself. This shows his love and his justice working together.

The most precious line is this: “Their blood will be precious in his sight.” Lives that seem small and ignored in human eyes are infinitely valuable in God’s eyes. This overturns our values. It is not status, ability, or achievement that counts; every person is treasured by God.
a: Cry out to God in hardship
Believe that God hears and will answer.
See people through God’s eyes
Honor the worth of every life.
Become a vessel of compassion
Take the initiative to care for and help those in need.
q: When I feel lonely and helpless, do I believe I am precious in God’s eyes?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for seeing my need and hearing my cry. When I am weak, rescue me; when I am helpless, hold me up. Give me also Your heart, to have compassion on others and help them, so that Your love may flow. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I am precious in God’s eyes. He watches over me and saves me, and I live out his compassion.

t: Accept One Another, to God’s Glory
v: Now the God of perseverance and of encouragement grant you to be of the same mind with one another according to Christ Jesus,
that with one accord you may with one mouth glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore accept one another, even as Christ also accepted you, to the glory of God.
b: This passage points to the source of unity: not human effort, but “the God of patience and of encouragement.” People differ in nature and background, and it is easy for differences and friction to arise. But God puts his patience and encouragement within us so that we can bear with one another. True unity is the overflow of life from God.

“Be of the same mind … according to Christ Jesus.” The standard of unity is not mutual compromise but following Christ. As Jesus accepted us, so we accept others. This is the way of self-denial: not insisting on ourselves but letting ourselves go. Only with selflessness is there true unity.

The result is “with one accord, with one mouth, glorify God.” When we are no longer centered on ourselves and let Jesus be King, relationships move from division to unity, from opposition to glory. Accepting one another is not the destination; glorifying God is the goal. The restoration of relationships ultimately points to the glory of God.
a: Receive patience from God
In relationships, depend on God rather than on your own emotions.
Take the initiative to accept others
Put down criticism and comparison, and see people with the love of Christ.
Pursue unity for its purpose
Let reconciliation in relationships bring glory to God.
q: Am I demanding that others change, or am I willing to accept them first with the love of Christ?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for accepting me first. Place Your patience and encouragement within me so that I can accept others. Help me follow Christ and live out a life of unity, so that all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I accept others, follow Christ, and glorify God with one accord and one mouth.

t: Feet First, Then the Waters Part
v: Joshua said to the children of Israel, “Come here, and hear the words of the LORD your God.”

Joshua said, “By this you shall know that the living God is among you, and that he will without fail drive the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Hivite, the Perizzite, the Girgashite, the Amorite, and the Jebusite out from before you.
Behold, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth passes over before you into the Jordan.
Now therefore take twelve men out of the tribes of Israel, for every tribe a man.

It shall be that when the soles of the feet of the priests who bear the ark of GOD, the Lord of all the earth, rest in the waters of the Jordan, that the waters of the Jordan will be cut off. The waters that come down from above shall stand in one heap.”
When the people moved from their tents to pass over the Jordan, the priests who bore the ark of the covenant being before the people,

and when those who bore the ark had come to the Jordan, and the feet of the priests who bore the ark had dipped in the edge of the water (for the Jordan overflows all its banks all the time of harvest),

the waters which came down from above stood, and rose up in one heap a great way off, at Adam, the city that is beside Zarethan; and those that went down toward the sea of the Arabah, even the Salt Sea, were wholly cut off. Then the people passed over near Jericho.

The priests who bore the ark of the LORD’s covenant stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan; and all Israel crossed over on dry ground, until all the nation had passed completely over the Jordan.
b: This passage reveals the key to faith: obey first, then see the miracle. God did not part the river first; he asked the priests to put their feet in the water first. And it was at the hardest time, when the Jordan was overflowing its banks. Faith is not waiting for circumstances to become easier; it is stepping out on God’s word.

The ark represents God’s presence, going ahead of the people. They were not forcing their own way; God himself was leading. When our focus is on Jesus and not on circumstances, fear is replaced by faith. When people are willing to obey, God shows his great power and turns the impossible into the possible.

In the end the people crossed on “dry ground.” They did not barely squeeze through; they crossed completely secure. God’s leading is sure and dependable. When we wholeheartedly obey the guidance of the Holy Spirit, we will experience the grace of God opening the way himself.
a: Take the first step of faith
Don’t wait for circumstances to change; obey God’s word first.
Let God go before you
Stop relying on your own analysis and follow God wholeheartedly.
Keep believing in difficulty
Even when circumstances are hard, trust that God will open a way.
q: Am I still standing on the riverbank watching, or am I willing to step into God’s promise?
pr: Heavenly Father, give me faith to obey Your word even in difficulty. Help me to walk not by sight but by Your promises. Let me experience the grace of You making a way, and follow You all my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I step out on God’s word, and God opens the way for me. I walk in his victory.

t: Having the Mind of Christ
v: doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.
Have this in your mind, which was also in Christ Jesus,
who, existing in the form of God, didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped,
but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men.
And being found in human form, he humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, yes, the death of the cross.
b: This passage reveals the core of a God-centered life: not exalting ourselves, but humbly giving ourselves up. By nature people compare, compete, and seek glory, but Paul says, “Do nothing through conceit.” The real problem is not outward behavior but the “self” sitting on the throne. When people center on themselves, division and conflict arise.

Paul’s answer is not a method but an example: “Have this in your mind, which was also in Christ Jesus.” Jesus was in the form of God, yet he did not grasp his rights; he emptied himself. He did not lose his identity; he laid down his rights. This is the essence of humility: letting God be God and letting man be man.

Jesus’ path went from glory to the cross, from the highest place to the lowest. He was obedient to death, showing that true victory is not control but self-giving. When we live this kind of life, we move from self-centeredness to selflessness, and Christ lives in us. Such a life brings true unity and glorifies God.
a: Lay down self-centeredness
Stop comparing and competing; learn to count others better than yourself.
Live in mutual care
Care not only for yourself but also for the needs of others.
Practice self-giving obedience
In everything, choose to obey God rather than insist on your own way.
q: Am I defending my rights, or living out the humility of Christ?
pr: Heavenly Father, place the mind of Christ within me so that I no longer exalt myself but learn humility and self-giving. Help me live out obedience in daily life, so that Jesus is King in me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I have the mind of Christ. I lay down myself and live in humility and obedience, letting the Lord be King in me.

t: Build the Altar First, Then the Temple
v: Some of the heads of fathers’ households, when they came to the LORD’s house which is in Jerusalem, offered willingly for God’s house to set it up in its place.
When the seventh month had come, and the children of Israel were in the cities, the people gathered themselves together as one man to Jerusalem.
In spite of their fear because of the peoples of the surrounding lands, they set the altar on its base; and they offered burnt offerings on it to the LORD, even burnt offerings morning and evening.
They kept the feast of booths, as it is written, and offered the daily burnt offerings by number, according to the ordinance, as the duty of every day required;

and afterward the continual burnt offering, the offerings of the new moons, of all the set feasts of the LORD that were consecrated, and of everyone who willingly offered a free will offering to the LORD.
From the first day of the seventh month, they began to offer burnt offerings to the LORD; but the foundation of the LORD’s temple was not yet laid.

They also gave money to the masons and to the carpenters. They also gave food, drink, and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre to bring cedar trees from Lebanon to the sea, to Joppa, according to the grant that they had from Cyrus King of Persia.
b: This passage shows us a spiritual order: first the altar, then the temple. When the people returned to Jerusalem, the first thing they did was not a construction project but the restoration of worship. Even though the temple had no foundation yet, they first built an altar in the old place and offered sacrifices to God. This reminds us that the foundation of life is not ministry but our relationship with God.

They gathered “as one man,” showing the power of unity. They were afraid of outside threats, yet they did not draw back; instead they worshiped God more steadfastly. True security is not found in circumstances but in the presence of God. When people fix their eyes on God, fear no longer rules.

Only then did they begin the actual building, giving willingly and preparing the materials. Worship leads to action; relationship leads to ministry. When the heart is aligned with God, ministry naturally falls into line. First life, then relationships, then ministry: this is God’s order.
a: Restore your relationship with God first
Build an altar of worship and prayer every day.
Worship even in fear
Don’t let circumstances keep you from drawing near to God.
Join the building willingly
Offer your time and resources to take part in God’s work.
q: Am I busy building outward things, or have I first built an altar with God?
pr: Heavenly Father, help me fix my focus on You and first restore my relationship with You. Let me keep worshiping You in every circumstance, and willingly join in the building You have entrusted to me. Let my life grow according to Your order. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I build the altar and worship God first, then give myself to building. When my life is aligned with God, my ministry is aligned too.

t: Reshaped in His Hands
v: The word which came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying,
“Arise, and go down to the potter’s house, and there I will cause you to hear my words.”
Then I went down to the potter’s house, and behold, he was making something on the wheels.
When the vessel that he made of the clay was marred in the hand of the potter, he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it.
Then the LORD’s word came to me, saying,
“House of Israel, can’t I do with you as this potter?” says the LORD. “Behold, as the clay in the potter’s hand, so are you in my hand, house of Israel.
b: God took Jeremiah to see a simple picture: a potter making a vessel. The clay is shaped in his hands according to his will. If the vessel is spoiled, the potter does not throw it away but makes it again. This shows God’s heart: he is not eager to discard us but willing to reshape us.

The key is not the clay but whether it is in the potter’s hands. When people leave God, they are like clay out of the potter’s hands, unable to take shape; when they are willing to entrust themselves, they can be formed into useful vessels. Many times we feel we have been “spoiled,” but in God’s hands there is no life that cannot start again.

“As seemed good to the potter to make it.” God’s shaping follows his will, not our preferences. This takes humility and obedience. Only with selflessness can we be shaped; only with obedience can we become useful. When we let Jesus be King and are led by the Holy Spirit, our lives move from brokenness to beauty.
a: Be willing to be shaped by God
Don’t resist God’s hand; let him remake your life.
Don’t be discouraged by failure
Even when you fall, believe that God can rebuild.
Obey God’s will
Lay down your own plans and accept God’s arrangement.
q: Am I resisting God’s hand, or am I willing to be a vessel in his hands?
pr: Heavenly Father, make me soft and willing to be shaped in Your hands. Forgive me for the times I have resisted Your leading, and remake my life so that I become a vessel that pleases You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I am being shaped in God’s hands; he makes me from broken pieces into a useful vessel.

t: My Help Comes From the Lord
v: I will lift up my eyes to the hills. Where does my help come from?
My help comes from the LORD, who made heaven and earth.
He will not allow your foot to be moved. He who keeps you will not slumber.
Behold, he who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
The LORD is your keeper. The LORD is your shade on your right hand.
The sun will not harm you by day, nor the moon by night.
The LORD will keep you from all evil. He will keep your soul.
The LORD will keep your going out and your coming in, from this time forward, and forever more.
b: This psalm begins with a question: “Where does my help come from?” We usually look to circumstances, resources, and abilities for the answer, but the psalmist immediately declares, “My help comes from Yahweh, who made heaven and earth.” Help is not found in created things but in the Creator. When our focus turns from the world to God, our hearts are steadied.

God’s protection is not temporary but constant. “He will neither slumber nor sleep.” He is never careless and never tired. By day or by night, in light or in darkness, God is watching over us. He does not protect from a distance; he is our shade “on your right hand,” close to our lives, ready to support us at any moment.

The final promise is complete: “your going out and your coming in … from this time forward, and forevermore.” This is not care for a season but care for a whole lifetime and into eternity. When we let Jesus be King and place ourselves in his hands, we live under his unbroken protection.
a: Adjust your focus
Stop depending on circumstances and turn to God as the source of help.
Rest in God’s care
Believe that he does not slumber, and learn to let go of anxiety.
Entrust every step
Whether coming or going, in big things or small, place it in God’s hands.
q: When I face difficulty, do I lift my eyes to the hills, or to God?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for being my help at all times. When I am weak, remind me to look to You instead of depending on circumstances. Let me rest in Your protection, believing that You are with me at all times and in all places. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: My help comes from the Lord. He keeps me, from this time forward and forevermore.

t: Still Looking Up in the Dark
v: If indeed you will magnify yourselves against me, and plead against me my reproach,
know now that God has subverted me, and has surrounded me with his net.
“Behold, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard. I cry for help, but there is no justice.
He has walled up my way so that I can’t pass, and has set darkness in my paths.
He has stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown from my head.
He has broken me down on every side, and I am gone. He has plucked my hope up like a tree.
He has also kindled his wrath against me. He counts me among his adversaries.
His troops come on together, build a siege ramp against me, and encamp around my tent.
b: This passage shows Job’s deepest pain. He suffered not only calamity but also the feeling that God had become his enemy. His prayers went unanswered, his way was blocked, and his future grew dark. This is the hardest time in the spiritual life: not outward difficulty, but the feeling that God is silent.

Job honestly spoke out the pain in his heart and did not pretend to be strong. This reminds us that we can be real before God. Faith is not suppressing our feelings but still turning to God in the dark. Even when we don’t understand, we don’t walk away. A relationship like that is more precious than any answer.

Although this passage ends in darkness, the whole book of Job lets us know that God did not leave. God’s work is often done in places we cannot see. When we feel trapped, we may in fact be in the process of being shaped. If our focus remains on Jesus and not on our feelings, we can walk through the darkness and into the light.
a: Be honest in pain
Don’t suppress your emotions; bring your true self to God.
Hold on in silence
Even if you feel God is not answering, don’t leave him.
Look up in the dark
Believe that God is still working, even when you cannot see it.
q: When I feel God is silent, do I move away from him, or do I still turn to him?
pr: Heavenly Father, when I am in darkness and confusion, hold up my heart so that I am not shaken by my feelings. Help me keep trusting You in pain, knowing that You have never left. Lead me through the darkness and into Your light. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Even in the dark, I still look up to God. He has not left, and he is still leading me.

t: Aligned With God First, Then Life Overflows
v: In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, in the first day of the month, the LORD’s word came by Haggai the prophet, to Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, saying,
Now therefore this is what the LORD of Armies says: ‘Consider your ways.

You have sown much, and bring in little. You eat, but you don’t have enough. You drink, but you aren’t filled with drink. You clothe yourselves, but no one is warm; and he who earns wages earns wages to put them into a bag with holes in it.’
“This is what the LORD of Armies says: ‘Consider your ways.
Go up to the mountain, bring wood, and build the house. I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified,” says the LORD.

“You looked for much, and, behold, it came to little; and when you brought it home, I blew it away. Why?” says the LORD of Armies, “Because of my house that lies waste, while each of you is busy with his own house.
Therefore for your sake the heavens withhold the dew, and the earth withholds its fruit.
I called for a drought on the land, on the mountains, on the grain, on the new wine, on the oil, on that which the ground produces, on men, on livestock, and on all the labor of the hands.”
b: This passage uncovers a spiritual problem: busyness without satisfaction. The people worked hard, yet harvested little; they ate without being filled, dressed without being warm, and their money seemed to be put into a bag with holes. The problem was not too little effort but the wrong focus. They looked after their own houses while God’s house lay in ruins.

Twice God says, “Consider your ways.” This is not a rebuke but a call. When the order of life is wrong, no amount of effort can bring true abundance. Outward lack reflects inward drift. When people center on themselves, they enter a cycle that spins without going anywhere.

God gives a clear way out: “Build the house; and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified.” When people put God first again and let God be King, blessing flows again. True abundance is not having more, but having a life aligned with God. God’s presence comes first, and then true provision.
a: Examine your life’s focus
Am I busy with my own affairs, or have I put God first?
Adjust your priorities
Seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness.
Rebuild your spiritual life
Restore prayer, worship, and your relationship with God.
q: Is the “house” of my life lying in ruins while I am busy with my own affairs?
pr: Heavenly Father, shine Your light on my life so I can see where I have drifted from Your heart. Forgive me for caring only about myself and neglecting Your presence. Help me realign with You and put You first, so that my life enters true abundance. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I align with God first and let him be King; my life enters true abundance and provision.

t: Living Out the Image of God
v: God said, “Let’s make man in our image, after our likeness. Let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the sky, and over the livestock, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.”
God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them.

God blessed them. God said to them, “Be fruitful, multiply, fill the earth, and subdue it. Have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the sky, and over every living thing that moves on the earth.”
God said, “Behold, I have given you every herb yielding seed, which is on the surface of all the earth, and every tree, which bears fruit yielding seed. It will be your food.
To every animal of the earth, and to every bird of the sky, and to everything that creeps on the earth, in which there is life, I have given every green herb for food;” and it was so.
God saw everything that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. There was evening and there was morning, a sixth day.
b: This passage reveals our most fundamental identity: we are made “in the image of God.” We are not here by accident; we were created with God’s image and likeness. This image is not outward appearance but the essence of life, able to connect with God and live out love and truth. When people leave God, they lose the expression of that image; when they return to God, their true identity is restored.

God not only created people but also gave them a mission: “Be fruitful, multiply, fill, subdue, have dominion.” This is not control but representing God on earth and living out his heart. A person’s true worth lies not in how much he owns but in whether he lives out the image of God. When we let Jesus be King, life is realigned with the purpose of creation.

Finally, God saw that everything was “very good.” This is God’s view: he sees people as good, valuable, and purposeful. When we look at ourselves through God’s eyes, we are neither self-deprecating nor proud, but return to our rightful place, letting God be God and man be man. This is true harmony and abundance of life.
a: Confirm your identity
I am not here by accident; I was made in God’s image.
Live out your mission
Express God’s character and stewardship in daily life.
See yourself through God’s eyes
Neither self-deprecating nor proud, but living within God’s heart.
q: Am I living out the image of God, or living in my own likeness?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for creating me in Your image. Restore in me the likeness that is Yours, so that I live out Your heart. Let Jesus be King in me, so that my life shows forth Your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I was created in God’s image. I live out his likeness and show forth his glory.

t: Standing Firm in Watchfulness
v: Be sober and self-controlled. Be watchful. Your adversary, the devil, walks around like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.
Withstand him steadfast in your faith, knowing that your brothers who are in the world are undergoing the same sufferings.
But may the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little while, perfect, establish, strengthen, and settle you.
To him be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.
b: This passage reminds us that spiritual warfare is real. The enemy does exist; he “walks around.” Like a lion he looks for someone to devour, especially those who are relaxed and not watchful. If we let our guard down in the spiritual life, we are easily devoured.

But what God gives us is not fear but a way: “Withstand him steadfast in your faith.” We stand not by our own analysis but by faith. When our eyes are fixed on Jesus, the enemy has no foothold. And we are not alone; our brothers and sisters are in the same battle, and by supporting one another we will be victorious.

Our final hope is in God, “the God of all grace.” Suffering is temporary, but glory is eternal. God himself perfects, establishes, and strengthens us. When we pass through trials, our lives are built up instead. This is the path from battle to victory.
a: Stay watchful
Don’t let your life grow slack; always be alert to your spiritual condition.
Resist with faith
Refuse doubt and stand on God’s word.
Hold on to eternal hope
See that suffering is temporary and glory is eternal.
q: Am I standing watchful in the Spirit, or have I unknowingly grown slack?
pr: Heavenly Father, help me stay watchful and give the enemy no opening. Give me steadfast faith so that I can stand in the battle. Let me see Your work in suffering and experience the strength and perfecting that You give. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I stand watchful and resist the enemy with faith. God himself strengthens me and gives me victory.

t: Store God’s Word in Your Heart
v: It shall happen, if you shall listen diligently to my commandments which I command you today, to love the LORD your God, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul,
that I will give the rain for your land in its season, the early rain and the latter rain, that you may gather in your grain, your new wine, and your oil.
I will give grass in your fields for your livestock, and you shall eat and be full.
Be careful, lest your heart be deceived, and you turn away to serve other gods and worship them;

and the LORD’s anger be kindled against you, and he shut up the sky so that there is no rain, and the land doesn’t yield its fruit; and you perish quickly from off the good land which the LORD gives you.
Therefore you shall lay up these words of mine in your heart and in your soul. You shall bind them for a sign on your hand, and they shall be for frontlets between your eyes.
You shall teach them to your children, talking of them when you sit in your house, when you walk by the way, when you lie down, and when you rise up.
You shall write them on the door posts of your house and on your gates;
that your days and your children’s days may be multiplied in the land which the LORD swore to your fathers to give them, as the days of the heavens above the earth.
b: This passage reveals the foundation of blessing: listen diligently to God’s word and love him with all your heart. Blessing is no accident; it begins with being aligned with God. When the people loved and served God, he sent the former and latter rain in season so that the land would yield. Outward provision comes from a right relationship with God within.

God also warned the people that the greatest danger is not circumstances but a heart that is “deceived.” Once the heart drifts, the steps drift, and finally people worship other gods. When we put security, money, or achievement in the place of God, these are the idols of our day. The problem is often not outward lack but an inward turning away.

Therefore God says to lay up his words in the heart and soul, and to teach the next generation. God’s word is not only to be heard at meetings; it is to be talked about sitting, walking, lying down, and rising up. When truth enters the family and daily life, blessing continues from generation to generation. Only when God’s word first enters the heart does life enter abundance.
a: Store up God’s word daily
Let the Bible be the standard for your thoughts and decisions.
Guard your heart carefully
Watch for whatever is taking God’s place.
Pass it on to the next generation
Talk about truth in the family and build a godly culture.
q: What is my heart full of? God’s word, or the voices of the world?
pr: Heavenly Father, make me love You and obey You, and keep Your word deep in my heart. Keep me from being deceived and from turning from the right path. Help me also pass the truth on to the next generation, so that my family becomes a place of blessing. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I store God’s word in my heart and love the Lord wholeheartedly. I walk the path of blessing and of passing it on.

t: Do Not Be Afraid—The Lord Still Reigns
v: This is the Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave him to show to his servants the things which must happen soon, which he sent and made known by his angel to his servant, John,
who testified to God’s word and of the testimony of Jesus Christ, about everything that he saw.
I turned to see the voice that spoke with me. Having turned, I saw seven golden lamp stands.
And among the lamp stands was one like a son of man, clothed with a robe reaching down to his feet, and with a golden sash around his chest.
His head and his hair were white as white wool, like snow. His eyes were like a flame of fire.
His feet were like burnished brass, as if it had been refined in a furnace. His voice was like the voice of many waters.
He had seven stars in his right hand. Out of his mouth proceeded a sharp two-edged sword. His face was like the sun shining at its brightest.
When I saw him, I fell at his feet like a dead man. He laid his right hand on me, saying, “Don’t be afraid. I am the first and the last,
and the Living one. I was dead, and behold, I am alive forever and ever. Amen. I have the keys of Death and of Hades.
b: This passage lets us see the glorified Christ. John was exiled on the island of Patmos, seemingly alone and suffering, yet heaven was opened to him. When he turned, he saw the Lord standing among the lampstands. This means the Lord has not left his church; he still reigns among his people.

The Lord’s appearance is full of majesty: eyes like a flame of fire, seeing through everything; a voice like many waters, full of authority; a face like the sun, full of glory. This Jesus is not a weak victim but the risen, victorious King. Though the world is in turmoil, the Lord is still on the throne.

When John fell down, the Lord first said, “Don’t be afraid!” For he is the first and the last, the one who was dead and is alive, and he holds the keys of Death and of Hades. This means that even the ultimate powers are in his hand. When we fix our eyes on Jesus, we can overcome fear. If our focus is on circumstances, we worry; if our focus is on the Lord, we have peace.
a: Keep turning to see the Lord
Don’t look only at circumstances; learn to fix your eyes on Jesus.
Hear the Lord’s voice in fear
Let “Do not be afraid” rise above the noise in your heart.
Live under his authority
Believe that your life and future are in the Lord’s hands.
q: Lately, have I seen more of my problems, or more of the reigning Lord?
pr: Heavenly Father, thank You for letting me see the glorious Jesus. When I am afraid, lay Your right hand on me and tell me not to fear. Let me know that You still reign, and lead me through every storm. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I am not afraid, for Jesus still reigns. He is the first and the last.

t: A Wise Heart Sees Eternity
v: A good name is better than fine perfume; and the day of death better than the day of one’s birth.
It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting; for that is the end of all men, and the living should take this to heart.
Sorrow is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the face the heart is made good.
The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise than for a man to hear the song of fools.
For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This also is vanity.
Surely extortion makes the wise man foolish; and a bribe destroys the understanding.
Better is the end of a thing than its beginning. The patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
Don’t be hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools.
Don’t say, “Why were the former days better than these?” For you do not ask wisely about this.
b: This passage overturns our instincts. People love feasting, laughter, and smooth times, but the Preacher says the house of mourning teaches wisdom instead. In joy we easily forget eternity; in sorrow we think about the nature of life. Death reminds us that we are limited, and that we need God.

“Better is the end of a thing than the beginning of it.” People often value the beginning, but God values the end. Starting is easy with enthusiasm; reaching the end takes patience. True maturity is not a sudden sprint but faithfulness to the end over a long road. Patience is better than pride, because pride is in a hurry to prove itself, while patience is willing to wait on God.

The passage also warns us not to live in nostalgia and complaint. “Why were the former days better than these?” is not a wise question. When people keep looking back, they lose today’s grace. A wise heart lives in God’s present tense, believing that God still reigns and still works today. Our focus is not on the past but on the Lord.
a: Learn wisdom from life’s limits
Reflect on the brevity of life and turn your heart toward eternity.
Practice patience to the end
Not only begin with passion, but faithfully finish the whole course.
Treasure the day God gives
Don’t dwell on the past; believe God is still working today.
q: Lately, has my heart been scattered by entertainment, or awakened by truth?
pr: Heavenly Father, give me a wise heart that understands that life is limited and learns to number my days. Help me endure to the end, not living in complaint about the past but following You today. Let me live every day with eternal value. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I have the heart of the wise. I think about eternity, endure to the end, and treasure the day God has given.
